title: Telemetry-driven density profiles and resize mentor for virtual tables
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Problem:
Current virtualized table experiences overwhelm users when they must manually tune density and column widths across datasets with varied content. Designers have shipped density presets and column resize handles, but we still see support tickets describing visual jitter, cramped content, and inconsistent keyboard interactions. Engineers want fewer one-off layout flags and a set of deterministic heuristics they can rely on across workloads.

Goal:
Create a design that (1) surfaces telemetry-driven density presets to end users and product teams, (2) introduces a transient 'Resize Mentor' — a lightweight in-UI coach that recommends snap targets and accessibility-friendly minimums while users drag column rails, and (3) standardizes the mapping between density tokens and virtualized measurement heuristics so runtime can apply consistent layout across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Proposed solution summary:
- Density Profiles: add three telemetry-driven presets (Comfort, Compact, Condensed) plus an Auto mode that uses model-informed heuristics (average row height, cell content truncation rate, common column width variance) to pick a recommended profile per table instance.
- Resize Mentor: when a user begins dragging a column edge, show a contextual mentor bubble with suggested snaplines (based on content fit and the currently selected density), an inline aria hint for screen readers describing the suggestion, and a keyboard-first fallback that announces suggested targets. Mentor persists for the first two drag interactions per session to avoid noise.
- Tokens & Measurement: introduce two new spacing tokens: token-space-table-breathe and token-space-table-compact-gap. Define row-height mapping (Comfort = 48px, Compact = 36px, Condensed = 28px) and create a deterministic formula for virtual row measurements used by the virtualization engine.
- Handoff: provide a Figma component set with three density variants, behavior spec for mentor states (initial, suggestion-accepted, suggestion-ignored), and a list of edge cases for ENG to implement (frozen columns, grouped headers, column pinning).

Design trade-offs considered:
- Persistent mentor vs transient: chose transient to reduce UI noise; will evaluate accept rate telemetry.
- Auto selection complexity: kept heuristics simple (3 signals) to keep runtime predictable and avoid privacy-sensitive heuristics.
- Snap granularity: chose coarse snap targets (fit-to-content, 1/3/2x heuristic) to limit frequent micro-adjustments that break virtualization caches.

Accessibility considerations:
- Mentor bubble must be keyboard reachable and announced via aria-live.
- Resize handles must expose explicit aria-labels with current width and suggested width.
- Modal or persistent overlays blocked for screen readers; mentor is non-modal and dismissible via Escape.

Acceptance criteria (design and measurable):
1) Figma library updated with density tokens and three table variants + mentor overlay components.
2) Interaction spec document describing drag lifecycle, keyboard interactions, and aria announcements.
3) Prototype validated in user tests (n=6 engineers and n=6 PMs) with success criteria: 80% can use Mentor to reach satisfactory column widths in under 2 attempts.
4) Telemetry plan defined: suggestion_shown, suggestion_accepted, suggestion_rejected, auto_density_chosen with anonymized payloads.
5) ENG implements deterministic mapping and supplies a small demo route for Console QA.

Links and artifacts:
- PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/RT-Table+Density+Mentor (design PRD draft)
- Figma (component kit): https://www.figma.com/file/AbCdEf/Table-Density-Mentor
- FigJam research notes: https://www.figma.com/file/Research/Resize-Mentor-Playbook
- Example GitHub PR for instrumentation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1289

Rollout plan:
- Week 0-1: Finalize designs and sign-off with Product + Accessibility (this ticket).
- Week 2: Deliver component tokens and specs to ENG (hand-off meeting + acceptance doc).
- Week 3-4: Ship behind feature flag with telemetry only; monitor suggestion_accept_rate and keyboard usage metrics.
- Week 5: Iterate based on telemetry and user feedback; enable by default if suggestion_accept_rate > 25% and no major regressions.

Developer notes for ENG:
- Provide a lightweight API hook for the Auto density decision so Console can surface the recommended profile without duplicating heuristics.
- Mentor should not mutate persisted user column width preferences automatically; behavior is opt-in on accept.
- Ensure virtualization cache keys include density token to avoid visual artifacts when density toggles.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to expose Auto density decision to external customers via Redwood API? (PM-212)
- Does Dedicated/Private want to respect telemetry-driven Auto? add an admin toggle for org-level defaults.
- Determine final thresholds for snap targets after ENG prototype (requires instrumentation).
